player_action: I'm fatigued from the barbarian rage ending. I charge the hobgoblin.
correct_ruling: A fatigued character can neither run nor charge, and takes -2 to Strength and Dexterity. The charge is not allowed.
srd_reference: AbilitiesandConditions.rtf > Conditions > Fatigued; ClassesI.rtf > Barbarian > Rage
common_wrong_rulings: Fatigue is a 5e exhaustion level with disadvantage on ability checks.

player_action: I'm fatigued and then forced-march into more fatigue. I'm at exhaustion level 2 now, right? Disadvantage on attacks?
game_state: Fatigued PC does something that would cause fatigue again.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no exhaustion levels. A fatigued character who does something that would normally cause fatigue becomes exhausted: half speed, -6 to Strength and Dexterity, can't run or charge. After 1 hour of complete rest, an exhausted character becomes fatigued.

player_action: How long do I need to rest to stop being fatigued after the rage?
correct_ruling: After 8 hours of complete rest, a fatigued character is no longer fatigued.
common_wrong_rulings: It ends at the end of the encounter.

player_action: I've been blinded by the glitterdust. What changes for me?
correct_ruling: Blinded: he can't see, takes -2 to AC, loses his Dex bonus to AC, moves at half speed, and takes -4 on most Strength- and Dexterity-based skill checks. All opponents effectively have total concealment (50% miss chance) relative to him.

player_action: I'm caught in a web spell and entangled. I'll cast magic missile.
game_state: Wizard entangled (not anchored question aside), wants to cast.
correct_ruling: An entangled character who tries to cast a spell must make a Concentration check (DC 15) or lose the spell. He also takes -2 on attacks, -4 Dex, moves at half speed (or not at all if anchored), and can't run or charge.

player_action: I'm nauseated, but drinking a potion is basically just a move action, right? It's one sip. Come on.
game_state: Nauseated PC wants to drink a potion of cure moderate wounds.
correct_ruling: No. A nauseated creature can take only a single move action per turn; it can't attack, cast, concentrate, or take other actions. Drinking a potion is a standard action, so it isn't allowed.
srd_reference: AbilitiesandConditions.rtf > Conditions > Nauseated; CombatII.rtf > Standard Actions > Use Special Ability / Activate Magic Item
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing it as a bonus action (5e).

player_action: I'm sickened from the troglodyte stench. Can I still cast?
correct_ruling: Yes. Sickened only imposes -2 on attack rolls, weapon damage rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks. (Nauseated is the condition that prevents casting.)
common_wrong_rulings: Confusing sickened with nauseated and forbidding actions.

player_action: My friend is dying at -6. I make a Heal check to stabilize him.
game_state: Ally at -6 hp; PC adjacent with Heal skill.
correct_ruling: A DC 15 Heal check (standard action) stabilizes a dying character. He remains unconscious at -6 but stops losing hit points.
srd_reference: SkillsII.rtf > Heal (First Aid); CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Stable Characters
common_wrong_rulings: Stabilizing also restores him to 1 hp.

player_action: The ogre hits my halfling with a sap for 15 nonlethal. I have 15 hp left. What happens? And what if it had been 16?
game_state: Halfling with 15 current hp, no prior nonlethal damage.
correct_ruling: When nonlethal damage equals current hit points, the character is staggered (only a single move or standard action each round). When it exceeds current hit points, the character falls unconscious. So 15 = staggered, 16 = unconscious.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Nonlethal Damage > Staggered and Unconscious
common_wrong_rulings: Nonlethal reduces hp like normal damage.

player_action: The bandit is helpless, tied up. I hit him with my sword. Any bonus?
game_state: Bound, helpless bandit; fighter adjacent with longsword.
correct_ruling: Melee attacks against a helpless defender get a +4 bonus, and the defender's Dex is treated as 0 (-5 modifier to AC). Ranged attacks get no special bonus beyond the Dex change. Rogues can sneak attack a helpless target.
common_wrong_rulings: Automatic critical hit on any hit (5e paralyzed).
Automatic hit without a full-round coup de grace.

player_action: The harpy is flying and gets paralyzed by the ghoul touch. What happens?
game_state: Winged harpy flying 30 ft up, paralyzed.
correct_ruling: A paralyzed winged creature flying in the air can't flap its wings and falls (taking falling damage). A paralyzed swimmer can't swim and may drown.

player_action: I'm at 0 hp, disabled. I want to lie still and pretend I'm dead so the bandits move on.
game_state: Disabled PC at 0 hp, bandits nearby.
correct_ruling: The rules don't specifically cover feigning death; the DM decides. A reasonable approach is a Bluff check opposed by the bandits' Sense Motive, with circumstance modifiers; staying still requires no strenuous action, so no hp is lost.
common_wrong_rulings: Automatic success because he's at 0 hp.
confidence_note: Judgment item; the SRD has no feign-death rule.

player_action: We marched for two days without sleeping. What penalties do I get?
game_state: Party has skipped sleep for 48 hours, no forced march beyond 8 hours/day.
correct_ruling: The SRD has no general sleep-deprivation rule (only forced-march and spellcaster rest requirements). The DM decides; imposing fatigued (possibly escalating to exhausted) is a common, defensible call.
srd_reference: Movement.rtf > Forced March (closest rule); AbilitiesandConditions.rtf > Fatigued
common_wrong_rulings: Inventing an exact RAW penalty table.
5e: exhaustion level per missed long rest.
confidence_note: Fairly sure no general sleep-deprivation rule exists in the SRD; forced march rules do apply if they marched more than 8 hours per day.

player_action: I'm stunned while balancing on a narrow ledge. Do I fall?
game_state: Rogue on a 6-inch ledge (Balance check normally required), stunned.
correct_ruling: The rules don't say directly whether a stunned creature falls from a ledge; it can't take actions and loses its Dex bonus to AC, so it can't make the move it was attempting. Whether it falls is a DM call; a common ruling is to require a Balance check or rule it holds still without moving.
common_wrong_rulings: Stunned has no effect on balance.
confidence_note: Judgment call; Balance text notes being attacked while balancing, but not stunned.

player_action: I'm a barbarian — raging means I just shrug off the fear from the dragon. I'm not shaken.
game_state: Barbarian 5 raging, failed Will save vs frightful presence (shaken).
correct_ruling: Rage grants +2 morale on Will saves (already applied); it doesn't grant fear immunity in the core rules. He failed, so he's shaken.
common_wrong_rulings: Re-rolling the save because of rage.

player_action: I've got 18 Con. In our last group we died at negative Con score. Can't I just keep fighting until -18?
correct_ruling: The core rule is death at -10 hp; negative-Con death is a house rule. By the rules he's dead (a DM may adopt a house rule, but that's a change to RAW).
common_wrong_rulings: Accepting the house rule as RAW.

player_action: My buddy is stable at -3. How does he wake up?
game_state: Stable, unconscious ally at -3 hp, no magical healing, nobody tending him.
correct_ruling: A stable character who hasn't been tended has a 10% chance each hour to become conscious (disabled); otherwise he loses 1 hp. If tended by someone with Heal, he doesn't lose hp; healing (magic or natural) is how hp returns.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Stable Characters and Recovery
confidence_note: Recall: unaided stable character each hour 10% chance to become conscious; if not, loses 1 hp. Check SRD wording for the tended case.

player_action: The gelatinous cube is in the room. I cast blindness on it.
correct_ruling: Oozes are blind (they have blindsight) and immune to gaze attacks, visual effects, illusions, and other attack forms that rely on sight; the blindness spell accomplishes nothing.
common_wrong_rulings: It gets a Fort save as normal.

player_action: I'm deafened from the thunderstone. Does that affect my spellcasting?
game_state: Sorcerer deafened, casting a spell with a verbal component.
correct_ruling: A deafened character has a 20% chance of spell failure when casting spells with verbal components; he also takes -4 on initiative and automatically fails Listen checks.
common_wrong_rulings: He can't cast verbal spells at all.
